title: 5 Quality Stocks To Buy On A Huge Dip
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garble several names and figures in places
summary: Carlson opens on the neocloud earnings bounce: CoreWeave rose 19% after reporting, its CEO saying the post-midterm political shift will not slow the cloud buildout, and Nebius rose 17% in sympathy. He then runs through five dip candidates. Nvidia is a BUY, flipping from UNCERTAIN on 9 November: at ~$174 and a 12.6x forward P/E, the 22% fall looks disproportionate to fundamentals, though he is not buying himself because his portfolio is already concentrated in the same industry. Fair Isaac is UNCERTAIN and wait-and-see: down 55% year to date to ~$700 from a $2,400 high, everything hinges on whether VantageScore takes serious market share. Uber is a CONDITIONAL_BUY at $60: he will add $10,000 if it drops to $60. Netflix is a CONDITIONAL_BUY below $60, softening from BUY: he will add $10,000 there, arguing YouTube engagement comparisons are apples-to-oranges because ambient, lo-fi and music streams count as watch time. Meta is a BUY, flipping from HOLD: he pushes back on Steve Eisman's off-balance-sheet-debt attack over the $27 billion Louisiana data centre (Meta owns 20% of the Beignet Investor LLC vehicle), saying everything is public and SEC-registered and Meta earns about $80 billion in operating income. Costco is a HOLD reiterated: it just declared a $30 special dividend, about a 3% yield and $13 billion, from roughly $21 billion of cash against about $4 billion of debt; he holds about $93,000, up roughly 2.7x.

calls.bull_case: Growth and margins hold and the stock re-rates from a cheap 12.6x multiple.
calls.bear_case: Scandal proves worse than expected for leadership/regulation, or growth/margins slip and the cheap multiple is deserved.
